approval.description: An approval code's tag (SPEC §7.2.1): tag = HMAC-SHA-256(secret, "tieroute link approval" || k || hpke), with k the new device's composite public key (device 5's) and hpke the HPKE public key above; code = the first 20 bytes of tag as 32 characters of uppercase Crockford base32, most significant bit first. §7.2.1 is still proposed.

bundle.description: A sealed link bundle (SPEC §7.2 step 4). HPKE base mode, RFC 9180, with KEM 0x647A (X-Wing: ML-KEM-768 + X25519), HKDF-SHA256, and AES-128-GCM (SPEC §3). info = "tieroute link bundle"; the associated data is the identifier's text as UTF-8 bytes. sealed = the 1,120-byte encapsulation || the AEAD ciphertext of JCS(link-bundle). Encapsulation is random, so this is one sealing among many: an implementation checks that it opens, not that it seals to the same bytes. The empty history means the same as none.
bundle.hpke_private_note: the 32-byte X-Wing private key (its seed), as RFC 9180's DeserializePrivateKey takes it

description: Linking a device in wire version 2 (SPEC §7.2, §3.2.2). The new device (device 5 of fork.json) parks its HPKE key with a link proof without a code, and later signs the typed confirmation code. Both proofs carry the new device's composite public key in k (it isn't in a chain yet) and a composite signature. The link code has room only for the Ed25519 component: the existing device checks that the last 32 bytes of k equal the device key in the code, and that SHA-256 of `hpke` equals the hash in the code. Confirmation-code normalization is unchanged from wire version 1 (../link.json).

full.rule: "link-" || lowercase base32 (no padding) of the Ed25519 component || SHA-256(HPKE public key), in groups of 4 joined by "-", then "@" || home

notice: Test vectors for Tieroute wire version 2 (SPEC version 2.0, draft). These keys are public: never use them for anything real.
proof_note: t = "link-proof", k = the new device's composite public key, body {id, code (normalized), ts}; the parked proof has hpke instead of code. The confirmation proof replaces the parked one on the homeserver, and the existing device seals the bundle to the HPKE key it fetched from the parked proof

signed_bundle.description: A signed link bundle (SPEC §7.2 step 4). sig is a `signed` object with t = "link-bundle", signed by device 1 (k = its Ed25519 component; the composite key is in the identity's chain), whose body is {id, device: SHA-256 of the new device's composite public key (device 5), hpke: SHA-256 of the HPKE public key in `bundle`, bundle: SHA-256 of JCS of the bundle without sig}. members maps each group in groups to its member identities. The new device refuses the bundle if the signature fails, if k isn't a current device other than itself, or if any of the three hashes differs. Sealing works as for `bundle`.
signed_bundle.plaintext_note: JCS(link-bundle) with sig: what would be sealed
